questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. the quietest .

__
 
• The given sentence refers to the quietness of the gentleman compared to others in the community.
 
• When comparing more than two things, we use the superlative form of the adjective, which is formed by adding "-est" to short adjectives.
 
• The correct superlative form of "quiet" is "the quietest".

Correct sentence: *The bishop sadly declared that the poor gentleman who was dead was **the quietest** of the community*.

• **Comparative form:**

 
 
• **Structure:** adjective + -er (for short adjectives) or more + adjective (for longer adjectives).
 
• **Example:** quieter or more quiet.
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare two things.
 
 
 
• **Superlative form:**
 
 
• **Structure: **adjective + -est (for short adjectives) or most + adjective (for longer adjectives).
 
• **Example: **quietest or most quiet.
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare three or more things.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Most probably, / he come / to office / next Tuesday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. he come .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is about a future event, so the correct form should be **"he will come"**.
 
• In English, to indicate a future event, we use the auxiliary verb **"will"** along with the base form of the main verb.
 
• The correct structure for this sentence should be **"Most probably, he will come to office next Tuesday."**.

Correct sentence: *Most probably, he **will come** to office next Tuesday*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Simple Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + base verb (he comes).
 
• **Example:** He comes to the office every day.
 
• **Usage: **Describes habitual actions.
 
 
 
• **Future Simple Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure: **Subject + will + base verb.
 
• **Example: **He will come to the office next Tuesday.
 
• **Usage: **Describes actions that will happen in the future.

questions.question:
Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the following options.

The food company promoted newly launched products at affordable prices.

options.text: The food company will be promoting newly launched products at affordable prices.
The food company promotes newly launched products at affordable prices.
The food company had promoted newly launched products at affordable prices.
The food company is promoting newly launched products at affordable prices.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The food company will be promoting newly launched products at affordable prices. .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of the** present simple tense**, which describes a habitual action.
 
• To convert a present simple sentence to the future continuous tense, we use the structure **"will be + present participle (verb-ing)"**.
 
• The future continuous tense describes actions that will be happening at a specific time in the future.

Correct sentence: *The food company will be promoting newly launched products at affordable prices.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Simple Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** The food company will promote newly launched products at affordable prices.
 
• **Usage: **Describes actions that will occur in the future.
 
 
 
• **Present Continuous Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure: **is/am/are + present participle (verb-ing).
 
• **Example: **The food company is promoting newly launched products at affordable prices.
 
• **Usage: **Describes actions that are currently happening.
 
 
</ul
